result_text:
Promotions now carry an optional description, and it comes back from all six listings you named plus the code lookup. The full suite had one failure, a bug in my new test, which I fixed. `PromotionTest` passes now, but I didn't rerun the full suite after that fix.

- **`schema.sql`**: added a nullable `description VARCHAR(200)` column to `promotion`.
- **`model/Promotion.java`**: added a `description` component at the end of the record. The record's javadoc describes it.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createPromotion` stores it, and the six promotion queries select it and map it: `findPromotionByCode`, `listPromotionsActiveOn`, `listPromotionsActiveOnInRegion`, `listPromotionsByCategory`, `findBestPromotion`, `listUnusedPromotions`.
- **`service/PromotionService.java`**: added a six-argument `createPromotion(..., category, description)`. The existing five-argument version delegates to it with a null description, so the many existing callers and `DemoScenario` are unchanged. A blank description is stored as null, the same way a blank category is.
- **`PromotionTest.java`**: added `returnsDescriptionWithPromotion`. It creates SUMMER with the description and PLAIN without one, then checks the description in each listing, in the best-promotion query, and in the code lookup.

The failure was my test's data: both promotions had 10%, so the best-promotion tie-break picked PLAIN. I gave PLAIN a 1% discount. Nothing is committed.
